Delighting the Ministerialists, he speedily faced an angry scene when he expressed the opinion that it was in the interests of the trade unions and employers to ascertain if the habit of learning how to qualify for unemployment benefit was not growing.

Boothby (Conservative) asked that in view of the restoration of the gold standard immediate steps be taken to facilitate the summoning of an international financial conference, including representatives of the central banks, with a view to further stabilising currencies on the lines contemplated by the Genoa resolutions.
Lt. Col. Guinness, Financial Secretary of the Treasury, replied that the Genoa resolutions contemplated not action by Government in the first place but a conference of central banks. He doubted if the time had yet come for this. He added that co-operation among the central banks was increasing.

label: text
text: The hostility to the silk impost developing in certain trade circles is enhanced by the customs ruling that articles containing any silk will be taxed 33 per cent. on the complete article. Hence it affects a wide range of goods like clothing lined or trimmed with silk.

label: text
text: A. Col. W. Guinness, defending the tax in the House of Commons, denied that silk was anything but a luxury. It was mixed with wool and cotton merely to increase the attractiveness and was in no wise economical to the poorer classes.

label: text
text: He cited as an example of the superiority of cotton the fact that ladies preferred the feet and tops of the stocking to which they hitched their suspenders not to be made of silk.

label: text
text: This sally was greeted with cheers and laughter and mock cries of "Oh!"

label: text
text: 11.- Col. Guinness scouted the suggestion that the price of "2s. 113'd." stockings would cost much more, nor would the tax appreciably affect the industry.

label: text
text: Mr. Snowdon's concluding thrust in the House of Commons yesterday was that Mr. Churchill would go down to posterity as the Chancellor who taxed silk stockings.

label: text
text: EARLIER CABLES.

label: text
text: The President of the Silk Association is of the opinion that the present proposals afford very little protection for the English manufacturer.

label: text
text: The "Daily Mail," in a leader, declares that the advantage Mr. Churchill will give to the Home artificial silk industry is much too small to compensate for the difficulties, expenses and delays of excise supervision. It says that artificial silk will be one of the greatest textile materials of the future. Even before this blow, with the exception of one firm, the industry was not progressing as fast as certain Continental competing countries.

label: paragraph_title

SOCIALIST AS POLICE
PRESIDENT.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Berlin, April 30.

label: text
text: The Prussian Cabinet has appointed as Police President in Berlin the Socialist Deputy, Herr Grezinski, a metal worker and ex-leader of the Workmen's and Soldiers' Council at Cassel at the outbreak of the revolution.

label: text
text: Herr Marx has telegraphed his congratulations to Marshal Hindenburg, expressing his sincerest wishes that the German people under his presidency will enjoy law and order at home and peace abroad; and hoping that Germany, by continuing a policy of peaceful international understanding, will soon recover her rightful position in the world.

label: text
text: [A Berlin message of April 18 stated, inter alia: 'With the Socialists given a quid pro quo in the shape of the election of Herr Braun to the Prussian Premiership on April 3, Dr. Marx, the Coalitionist candidate, seems to be assured' of the Socialist support at the Presidential contest against 'Filed-Marshal Hindenburg.... Addressing an audience of 20,000, Dr. Marx; presidential candidate of the Republic Bloc, said that Germany must make sacrifices in order to maintain peace and secure it on the Western frontier. Nevertheless the Franco-German understanding was a valuable political aim, but the acceptance of the security pact as regards the West afforded all the more reason why Germany must remember her unnatural frontier conditions in the East and the social affinity binding them to Austria. Germany must again put forward her aim to national union with Austria and the resurrection of a great Germany.]

label: paragraph_title
text: WILL GO HALF WAY.

label: paragraph_title
text: RUSSIANS AND THEIR CREDITORS.

label: text
text: Mr. Stanford Talbot has resigned from the executive of the Association of British Creditors of Russia of which he was the first President. He intends to form an Anglo-Russian Conciliation Association to protest against the negative policy adopted to Russia. He is convinced that the Russians are willing to go over half way to meet their British creditors.

label: text
text: Mr. Talbot says that the British Government, the Association of British Creditors of Russia and the majority of Anglo-Russian industrial, merchant and banking interests have been systematically trying to drive the Anglo-Russian team with the cart before the horse, Russia must be helped if they want her to help them.

label: text
text: Mr. Talbot holds the opinion that it might be an agreeable surprise for British creditors if it could be made possible for the Soviet to be invited to state what it is prepared to do for creditors if a British loan of £100,000,000 could be made to Russia on a fair security.

label: paragraph_title
text: Chinese Take Part In Colourful Scenes.

label: text
text: The Prince of Wales is receiving a most enthusiastic welcome from all sections of the community in the capital of South Africa.

label: text
text: MEMORABLE GATHERING.

label: text
text: The warmth of the Prince of Wales's welcome eclipsed all South African traditions. Every window and balcony was crowded; the occupants adding their quota of roaring cheers to those of the massed crowds in the streets.

label: paragraph_title
text: WHERE HE IS NOW.

label: vision_footnote
text: Our map shows Capetown and the route the Prince follows during his inland travels.

label: text
text: of Athlone and Princess Alice boarded the Repulse at ten this morning, and an hour later the Prince of Wales landed from the pinnace and was welcomed by Premier Hertzog and members of the cabinet, the Speaker and the President of the Senate, the Archbishop of South Africa, General Smuts and Sir Thomas Smartt. Enthusiastic crowds joined in the welcome as the sun broke out brightly.

label: text
text: A luncheon in the City Hall at which the Mayor and the Council officially welcomed the Prince was attended by 500 guests.

label: text
text: This was the most representative gathering in Capetown's history.

label: text
text: The Mayor dwelt on the assurance of a loyal reception for the Prince all over the country.

label: text
text: The proceedings concluded by the Assembly rising and singing, "For He's a Jolly Good Fellow!"

label: text
text: Among the addresses presented to the Prince of Wales on the grand parade this afternoon were those of Indian, Chinese, Malay and other Moslem bodies, as well as the “Cape coloured” committees.”

label: text
text: Everywhere the coloured population demonstrated its loyal enthusiasm.

label: text
text: These thronged the outskirts of the grand parade and formed a vast concourse on Green Point common where the Prince reviewed the coloured Church. Lads' Brigade.

label: paragraph_title

STEAMER WRECKED.
(Reuter's Service.)

label: paragraph_title
text: Shanghai, April 30.

label: text
text: T.ie Chinese steamer Shun Chong, owned by the Yung Foong Company, bound for. Wenchow from Shanghai, has been wrecked off Tungchi Island, off Haimen. The accident occurred in a dense fog. Reports received to-day state that all hands were saved. The rescue was performed by a party of Chekiang water police, summoned to the scene by distress signals. The loss is estimated at one million dollars. The vessel's compradore is reported to have died from injuries received while rushing on deck, while the vessel was sinking.

label: text
text: London, April 30.—About forty per cent. of the Bibles published are sold in China, it is disclosed in the annual report of the British and Foreign Bible Society. Over ten million volumes were issued in the course of the year.—Reuter.
